title: Introduce prefill-qc: validation harness and CLI for batch/cache/quant templates
author: Ethan Chen
release_notes: Adds a new CLI (redwood prefill-qc) to validate prefill/batching/cache/quantization templates against unit-econ and latency SLOs. Includes smoke workload generator and a templated report format for safe rollbacks.
description:
Motivation: teams frequently commit prefill/batching/cache/quant templates that are safe in test but regress latency or unit economics in production edge cases. This PR introduces `prefill-qc`, a lightweight validation harness and CLI that runs deterministic smoke scenarios and cost-unit checks against templates before they are promoted.

What this includes: a CLI (cmd/prefill-qc) with commands: validate, lint, report; a deterministic smoke-workload generator that simulates cold/hot prefixes and burst traffic; an evaluation module that computes unit-econ deltas (cost_per_1M_tokens, p95_latency_delta, throughput_pct) and applies safety gates; auto-suggested rollback actions (lower batch_size, promote cached_prefill, fallback quant_profile) when thresholds are breached. Templates-as-code support serializes template diffs and produces an exportable JSON report that ops can attach to Linear/Jira.

Key user flows: 1) local developer run `redwood prefill-qc validate templates/my-tenant.yaml --dry-run` to get a compact report, 2) CI step (infra/ci/prefill-qc.yml) that runs the harness against PR changes and fails the job if unit-econ regressions exceed tolerances, 3) ops-run `redwood prefill-qc report --format=html` to produce a human-friendly bundle for rollbacks.

Design notes: the harness intentionally uses small, repeatable synthetic inputs (short sequences + a mix of cache-hit ratios) to avoid long noisy runs while still surfacing regressions tied to batching/cache interplay and quantization fallbacks. Safety gates are configurable per-tenant via policy files and are conservative by default (p95 latency +10% or cost +15%).

Backward compatibility: no runtime behavior changes. This is an opt-in validation tool used before template promotion. The PR adds no host runtime dependencies.

Checklist:
- [x] CLI scaffold and new command registration
- [x] Evaluation engine with unit-econ metrics
- [x] Smoke workload generator (deterministic seeds)
- [x] CI integration (prefill-qc.yml)
- [x] Docs and example templates (docs/prefill-qc.md)
- [x] Unit and integration tests

Risks and mitigations: the primary risk is false positives in CI for low-traffic tenants. Mitigation: default tolerances are wide and the CI job exposes a `--allow-delta` override for experimental branches.

Related: ties into ENG-6120 (tenant prefill safety) and PM-332 (unit-econ alerts).
